questions.clue: Rotate which subset is held out, refit on the rest, and average the held-out scores.
questions.explanation: Changing the validation fold lets each observation contribute an out-of-fit score.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 116, Cross-validation

questions.clue: The chance a value is missing is independent of all observed and unobserved values.
questions.explanation: Under MCAR, neither observed nor missing values predict which records are incomplete.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 279, Missing completely at random (MCAR)

questions.clue: Split the population into disjoint groups and draw a separate random sample from each group.
questions.explanation: Sampling within every stratum guarantees representation of each stratum when allocations are positive.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 415, Stratified random sampling

questions.clue: A second analyst gets the same tables using the original data and analysis code.
questions.explanation: Computational reproducibility concerns rerunning the original workflow with the original inputs.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research UC Berkeley STAT C245C, Fall 2018 syllabus, p. 2, Computationally reproducible research. https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~sandrine/Teaching/syllabus_PHC240C_F18.pdf

questions.clue: A regression drops each row that has any missing value among its fitted variables.
questions.explanation: Complete case analysis fits the model using records complete for the variables it needs.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 94, Complete case analysis

questions.clue: Randomly pick six schools and interview every student in those schools.
questions.explanation: The school is the sampling unit, and every student in a chosen school is included.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 87, Cluster sampling

questions.clue: A collaborator needs the exact analysis script used before three later edits. What helps retrieve it?
questions.explanation: A recorded revision identifies the exact code to restore.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §2, Version control. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#version-control

questions.clue: Which setting helps recreate the same random train/test split with unchanged code and software?
questions.explanation: A fixed seed lets the same pseudorandom process reproduce the split under the same conditions.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley R Bootcamp, Module 9, Some ideas for improving reproducibility. https://computing.stat.berkeley.edu/r-bootcamp-fall-2022/modules/module9_workflows

questions.clue:
n / N
n sampled units from a population of N
questions.explanation: This is the fraction of population units included in the sample.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 506, §6.1, Stratified Sampling. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat506/Lesson06

questions.clue:
1 / πᵢ
πᵢ is unit i’s inclusion probability
questions.explanation: Units with smaller inclusion probabilities have larger base weights.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 208, Horvitz–Thompson estimator University of Maryland SURV 701, Winter 2018 syllabus, p. 1, Short Course Description. https://jpsm.umd.edu/sites/jpsm.umd.edu/files/syllabi/SURV701_Online_Winter2018_v1.pdf

questions.clue: For every missing xᵢ, set xᵢ = x̄ observed.
questions.explanation: Every missing entry in the variable receives the same observed mean.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 509, Lesson 1, Missing Data. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat509/Lesson01

questions.clue:
sqrt[Σᵢ(yᵢ − ŷᵢ)² / n]
Evaluate on n held-out cases.
questions.explanation: The square root returns the squared prediction loss to the outcome’s units.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 20, Overfitting, Mean square error: another metric for evaluation. https://stat20.berkeley.edu/spring-2025/5-prediction/03-overfitting/notes.html

questions.clue: Given the observed data, missingness varies with observed values and is independent of the unobserved values.
questions.explanation: MAR allows systematic differences explained by observed data.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 279, Missing at random (MAR)

questions.clue: A fitted model captures quirks of its training data that hurt accuracy on new observations.
questions.explanation: A model can improve training fit while worsening out-of-sample predictions.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 314, Overfitted models

questions.clue: Fill a missing entry with a recorded value from a comparable respondent in the same survey.
questions.explanation: The replacement comes from an observed donor in the current survey.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 208, Hot deck

questions.clue: After sampling, adjust weights so the weighted counts for age groups match known population counts.
questions.explanation: Poststratification uses known population group sizes to adjust estimates after data collection.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 506, §6.1, Stratified Sampling. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat506/Lesson06

questions.clue: Fit once on 70% of the records and score the model once on the unused 30%.
questions.explanation: The one reserved test subset supplies the prediction score.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 207, Holdout estimate

questions.clue: Even within each recorded age group, people with higher actual income skip the income question more often.
questions.explanation: Missingness still depends on the very value that would have been recorded.
questions.reference: University of Pennsylvania EPID 702, Spring 2021 syllabus, p. 3, Missing data 1–2. https://www.med.upenn.edu/bgs/assets/user-content/documents/spring-2021-courses/21a-epid-702-syllabus.pdf Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 218, Informative missing values

questions.clue: A citywide address list omits every apartment in a new district. What problem arises before sampling?
questions.explanation: Residents at absent addresses have no chance to enter the sample through this frame.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 377, Sampling frames Penn State STAT 506, §11.1, Nonsampling Errors. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat506/Lesson11

questions.clue: The same script gives a different result after a package upgrade. What record helps restore the old setup?
questions.explanation: A versioned environment file records the software and dependencies needed to rerun the analysis.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue:
−2ℓ̂ + 2k
ℓ̂ is the maximized log likelihood, k the parameter count.
questions.explanation: The 2k term penalizes added parameters when comparing fits.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 10, Akaike’s information criterion (AIC)

questions.clue:
−2ℓ̂ + k log(n)
k parameters and n independent observations
questions.explanation: BIC uses a complexity penalty that grows with the log of the sample size.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 37, Bayesian information criterion (BIC). Gelman, Hwang and Vehtari, Understanding predictive information criteria for Bayesian models, §3.7, Bayesian information criterion. https://stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/waic_understand3.pdf

questions.clue:
1 − n/N
For the variance of a mean under simple random sampling without replacement.
questions.explanation: The correction reduces the variance as the fraction sampled increases.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 166, Finite population correction Penn State STAT 506, §1.3, Estimation of Population Mean and Total under SRS. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat506/Lesson01
questions.convention: This is the variance multiplier when population variance uses denominator N − 1. The standard-error multiplier is its square root.

questions.clue:
Σᵢ wᵢyᵢ / Σᵢ wᵢ
Use the supplied survey weights wᵢ.
questions.explanation: Dividing the weighted total by the sum of the weights returns a mean on the original scale.
questions.reference: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, Software for Statistical Analysis of Sample Survey Data, weighted mean. https://www.hcp.med.harvard.edu/statistics/survey-soft/docs/blc_eob.html University of Maryland SURV 701, Winter 2018 syllabus, p. 1, Short Course Description. https://jpsm.umd.edu/sites/jpsm.umd.edu/files/syllabi/SURV701_Online_Winter2018_v1.pdf

questions.clue: What describes a smoother model gaining stability across training samples while introducing more systematic error?
questions.explanation: Smoothing can reduce prediction variance while increasing squared bias.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 45, Bias/variance tradeoff

questions.clue: For each pairwise correlation, retain all records with both variables present, even when other variables are missing.
questions.explanation: Different correlations may be based on different subsets of records.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 27, Available case analysis

questions.clue: What compares an estimator’s variance under its actual survey design with the variance under a same-size simple random sample?
questions.explanation: A value above one signals lower precision than the simple-random-sample benchmark.
questions.reference: University of Maryland SURV 701, Winter 2018 syllabus, p. 1, Short Course Description. https://jpsm.umd.edu/sites/jpsm.umd.edu/files/syllabi/SURV701_Online_Winter2018_v1.pdf University of Michigan Survey Research Center, Cross-Cultural Survey Guidelines, Sample Design Appendix C, Design effect. https://ccsg.isr.umich.edu/chapters/sample-design/appendix-c/

questions.clue: An executable report interleaves analysis code and narrative so code regenerates tables in place.
questions.explanation: Executable documents keep the explanation and the generating code together.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: Start with an intercept. At each step add the predictor giving the largest qualifying fit improvement.
questions.explanation: Forward selection grows the model by adding predictors one at a time.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 171, Forward selection procedure

questions.clue: Refit after assuming missing outcomes are successively 2, 5, and 10 points below MAR predictions. What is the purpose?
choices: Identify missing values from the data
questions.explanation: Varying an untestable assumption shows how much it could change the result.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 388, Sensitivity analysis University of Pennsylvania EPID 702, Spring 2021 syllabus, p. 3, Missing data 1–2. https://www.med.upenn.edu/bgs/assets/user-content/documents/spring-2021-courses/21a-epid-702-syllabus.pdf

questions.clue: Within each age group, double respondents’ base weights where half of sampled people replied.
questions.explanation: Dividing by the within-group response rate adjusts for represented nonrespondents.
questions.reference: University of Maryland SURV 701, Winter 2018 syllabus, p. 1, Short Course Description. https://jpsm.umd.edu/sites/jpsm.umd.edu/files/syllabi/SURV701_Online_Winter2018_v1.pdf Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 305, Non-response

questions.clue: A colleague notices hand-edited data cells cannot be traced. What change makes every correction repeatable?
choices: Export the final data as CSV
questions.explanation: A script records each transformation and can reapply it to the original data.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley R Bootcamp, Module 9, Some ideas for improving reproducibility. https://computing.stat.berkeley.edu/r-bootcamp-fall-2022/modules/module9_workflows

questions.clue:
Ū + (1 + 1/m)B
Ū is mean within-imputation variance, B is between-imputation variance.
questions.explanation: The formula combines within- and between-imputation uncertainty and adjusts for a finite m.
questions.reference: Duke University, Missing Data lecture, Total variance. https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~fl35/teaching/440-19F/decks/cs05_2_deck.html#total-variance
questions.convention: m is the number of imputations, at least two.

questions.clue:
Σᵢ∈s yᵢ / πᵢ
πᵢ is the inclusion probability for sampled unit i.
questions.explanation: The total sums each sampled value multiplied by the inverse of its inclusion probability.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 208, Horvitz–Thompson estimator

questions.clue:
λ Σⱼ ∣βⱼ∣ with λ > 0
βⱼ are regression slopes.
questions.explanation: The absolute-value penalty can set some fitted slopes exactly to zero.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 242, Lasso
questions.convention: The intercept is excluded from this penalty. Elastic net here means a mix of positive L1 and positive L2 penalties.

questions.clue:
Σᵢ(pᵢ − yᵢ)² / n
yᵢ is 0 or 1 and pᵢ is the predicted chance of 1.
questions.explanation: The binary Brier score is mean squared error for probability forecasts against 0–1 outcomes.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 64, Brier score
questions.convention: Uses the single-event binary form with range 0 to 1.

questions.clue: You have a raw data file. Which record tells you where that exact edition came from?
questions.explanation: Source and version identify the input even when a newer file has the same name.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: Create five plausible complete datasets, fit the same model on each, and combine the estimates.
questions.explanation: Multiple completed datasets carry uncertainty about missing values into the analysis.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 291, Multiple imputation

questions.clue: A feature selector uses every outcome before a train/test split. What threatens the test score?
questions.explanation: The selected features already reflect outcomes from the intended test split.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 154, Lab 4, Cross Validation, data leakage and pipelines. https://stat154.berkeley.edu/fall-2026/labs/lab4_cross_val/lab4_presentation_2026.html

questions.clue: A probability sample comes from one city’s property-owner list. Which group does that frame directly cover?
questions.explanation: The sampling frame determines who can be sampled by design.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 377, Sampling frames

questions.clue: A sampled household provides no answers at all.
questions.explanation: Unit nonresponse leaves the sampled unit without an interview.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 305, Non-response University of Maryland SURV 701, Winter 2018 syllabus, p. 1, Short Course Description. https://jpsm.umd.edu/sites/jpsm.umd.edu/files/syllabi/SURV701_Online_Winter2018_v1.pdf

questions.clue: A sampled household is interviewed but leaves the income field blank.
questions.explanation: Item nonresponse leaves an individual question unanswered.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 225, Item non-response

questions.clue: How do we name a model’s prediction error measured on the records used to fit it?
questions.explanation: The records used for model fitting define the training set.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 20, Overfitting, Mean square error: another metric for evaluation. https://stat20.berkeley.edu/spring-2025/5-prediction/03-overfitting/notes.html

questions.clue: A separate team repeats the same research question with newly collected data.
questions.explanation: Independent replication asks whether the conclusion recurs in another dataset.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: A source replaces its file each month. Which practice lets a collaborator recover the exact release used?
questions.explanation: Archiving and documenting the release identifies the exact input to the analysis.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research UC Berkeley R Bootcamp, Module 9, Some ideas for improving reproducibility. https://computing.stat.berkeley.edu/r-bootcamp-fall-2022/modules/module9_workflows

questions.clue: A researcher wants manuscript plots to update every time the raw inputs change. What should generate them?
questions.explanation: The plotting script can regenerate figures from updated inputs.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: Replace each missing weight with a single prediction from a model using height and age.
questions.explanation: Regression imputation uses related observations to generate a fitted value for each missing entry.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 509, Lesson 1, Missing Data. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat509/Lesson01

questions.clue: Pick a random start among the first ten addresses, then visit every tenth address.
questions.explanation: A random start and a fixed interval select the addresses.
questions.reference: University of Michigan Survey Research Center, Cross-Cultural Survey Guidelines, Sample Design, Appendix C. https://ccsg.isr.umich.edu/chapters/sample-design/appendix-c/

questions.clue:
r / e
All e sampled units are known eligible, and r completed an interview.
questions.explanation: This simplified response rate counts complete interviews among eligible sampled units.
questions.reference: University of Michigan Survey Research Center, Cross-Cultural Survey Guidelines, Sample Design, Appendix D. https://ccsg.isr.umich.edu/chapters/sample-design/appendix-d/
questions.convention: All units are known eligible. Partial interviews are excluded under this simplified definition.

questions.clue:
N / n
Select n units from an ordered list of N, where N is a multiple of n.
questions.explanation: The ratio gives the fixed step after selecting a random start.
questions.reference: University of Michigan Survey Research Center, Cross-Cultural Survey Guidelines, Sample Design, Appendix C. https://ccsg.isr.umich.edu/chapters/sample-design/appendix-c/

questions.clue:
Σᵢ(yᵢ − ŷᵢ)² / n
Evaluate on n held-out outcomes.
questions.explanation: Each held-out error is squared before averaging.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 20, Overfitting, Mean square error: another metric for evaluation. https://stat20.berkeley.edu/spring-2025/5-prediction/03-overfitting/notes.html

questions.clue:
Rᵢ = 1 if yᵢ is recorded, and 0 otherwise.
What does Rᵢ encode?
questions.explanation: The indicator records whether that outcome is observed.
questions.reference: Duke University, Missing Data lecture, Missing data mechanisms and methods. https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~fl35/teaching/440-19F/decks/cs05_2_deck.html
questions.convention: R = 1 denotes observed here. Some sources reverse the coding.

questions.clue: The objective retains each partial record and integrates the joint density over its missing values.
questions.explanation: Integrating out missing values gives the density of what was actually observed.
questions.reference: Duke University, Missing Data lecture, Missing data mechanisms and methods. https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~fl35/teaching/440-19F/decks/cs05_2_deck.html Duke University STA 440, Missing Data (2), The EM algorithm. https://www2.stat.duke.edu/courses/Spring25/sta440.001/slides/missing-data-2.html

questions.clue: Compare every candidate predictor combination of a given size before choosing one at that size.
questions.explanation: Best subset selection searches all candidate subsets within each model size.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 462, §11.3, Best Subsets Regression, Adjusted R-Sq, Mallows Cp. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat462/node/197/

questions.clue: A number attached to a population unit gives the chance it appears at least once in the sample.
questions.explanation: The first-order inclusion probability concerns selection at least once across the full design.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 214, Inclusion probability Penn State STAT 506, Lesson 3, Unequal Probability Sampling. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat506/Lesson03

questions.clue: A plot needs cleaned data, and cleaning needs a raw file. What should the workflow record?
choices: Which figures appeared in the abstract
questions.explanation: Recording input dependencies allows the steps to run in the right order.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: Begin with five predictors and remove the weakest qualifying predictor at each step.
questions.explanation: Backward elimination starts with the full model and removes one term at a time.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 897D, §4.1, Variable Selection for the Linear Regression Model. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat857/node/45/

questions.clue: All tuning is complete. Which data should give the final estimate of performance on unseen cases?
questions.explanation: An untouched test set avoids using its outcomes to choose the model it evaluates.
questions.reference: Harvard University, Introduction to Data Science, Chapter 29, Cross validation. https://rafalab.dfci.harvard.edu/dsbook/cross-validation.html

questions.clue: Select ten blocks at random, then randomly sample households separately in each chosen block.
questions.explanation: Blocks are selected first, followed by households within them.
questions.reference: University of Maryland SURV 701, Winter 2018 syllabus, p. 1, Short Course Description. https://jpsm.umd.edu/sites/jpsm.umd.edu/files/syllabi/SURV701_Online_Winter2018_v1.pdf Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 87, Cluster sampling

questions.clue: For a missing outcome, find observed cases with similar fitted values and draw an actual outcome from them.
questions.explanation: The fitted values identify candidate donors, and a donor’s observed outcome supplies the fill.
questions.reference: Duke University, Missing Data lecture, Missing data mechanisms and methods. https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~fl35/teaching/440-19F/decks/cs05_2_deck.html

questions.clue:
λ Σⱼ βⱼ² with λ > 0
βⱼ are regression slopes.
questions.explanation: Squaring the slopes gives a smooth penalty that shrinks large coefficients.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 370, Ridge regression Penn State STAT 508, Lesson 6, Regression Shrinkage Methods. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson06.html
questions.convention: Elastic net here includes a positive absolute-value penalty as well as a positive squared penalty.

questions.clue:
Σᵢ ∣yᵢ − ŷᵢ∣ / n
Evaluate on n held-out outcomes.
questions.explanation: Absolute values prevent positive and negative prediction errors from cancelling.
questions.reference: Stan User’s Guide, Held-Out Evaluation and Cross-Validation, Stan implementation with random folds. https://mc-stan.org/docs/2_36/stan-users-guide/cross-validation.html

questions.clue:
Σᵢwᵢ I(yᵢ=1) / Σᵢwᵢ
Survey weights wᵢ are positive.
questions.explanation: The formula divides the weighted count of target outcomes by the total weight.
questions.reference: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, Software for Statistical Analysis of Sample Survey Data, weighted mean. https://www.hcp.med.harvard.edu/statistics/survey-soft/docs/blc_eob.html

questions.clue:
Σⱼ Q̂ⱼ / m
Q̂ⱼ is the same effect estimated in completed dataset j.
questions.explanation: Rubin’s rules average the completed-data point estimates.
questions.reference: Duke University, Missing Data lecture, Missing data mechanisms and methods. https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~fl35/teaching/440-19F/decks/cs05_2_deck.html

questions.clue: With strong shrinkage, why can effective degrees of freedom be lower than the number of fitted slopes?
questions.explanation: A penalty limits how freely the fitted values can respond to the data.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 508, Lesson 6, Regression Shrinkage Methods. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat508/Lesson06.html

questions.clue: How does uncertainty generally change when some originally observed values are removed from the same model analysis?
choices: Information about the target must increase
Information is unaffected by any missingness
Information about the target can decrease
questions.answer: Information about the target can decrease
questions.explanation: Missing values can contribute less information than the same values would contribute if observed.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 280, Missing information principle

questions.clue: Before sampling, choose per-draw probabilities based on known community populations.
questions.explanation: Under PPS, a larger community size produces a proportionally larger per-draw probability.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 506, Lesson 3, Unequal Probability Sampling. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat506/Lesson03

questions.clue: What connects a reported table to the exact inputs and ordered transformations that produced it?
questions.explanation: Provenance tracks how the output follows from its source data and processing history.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue: After examining the test errors, someone tunes the penalty until test error improves. What has happened?
choices: The test error became training error
The test set became a tuning set
questions.answer: The test set became a tuning set
questions.explanation: Repeated selection by test performance incorporates the test results into model development.
questions.reference: Harvard University, Introduction to Data Science, Chapter 29, Cross validation. https://rafalab.dfci.harvard.edu/dsbook/cross-validation.html

questions.concept: effective sample size from design effect
questions.clue: A team reports how many simple-random-sample observations would match its complex survey’s precision. What is that count?
questions.explanation: The effective size is the sample size under simple random sampling that would give comparable precision.
questions.reference: University of Michigan Survey Research Center, Cross-Cultural Survey Guidelines, Sample Design Appendix C, Design effect. https://ccsg.isr.umich.edu/chapters/sample-design/appendix-c/
questions.convention: Uses the usual large-population approximation for variance proportional to 1/n.

questions.clue: An analyst fills all missing ages with the observed mean. What typically happens to the sample spread of age?
questions.explanation: Identical mean fills add zero squared deviations while increasing the variance denominator.
questions.reference: Duke University, Missing Data lecture, Missing data mechanisms and methods. https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~fl35/teaching/440-19F/decks/cs05_2_deck.html
questions.convention: Assumes at least two observed values with positive variance and at least one mean fill.

questions.clue: How can a team detect code that only works because a package is installed on the original analyst’s laptop?
choices: Run in a newly restored environment
questions.answer: Run in a newly restored environment
questions.explanation: A fresh environment built from the declared dependencies can reveal packages that were never recorded.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 243, Unit 4, §4, Reproducible research. https://stat243.berkeley.edu/fall-2024/units/unit4-goodPractices.html#reproducible-research

questions.clue:
1 − [SSE/(n−k−1)] / [SST/(n−1)]
n rows and k slopes in a regression with intercept.
questions.explanation: The residual degrees of freedom account for how many slopes were estimated.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 462, §11.3, Best Subsets Regression, Adjusted R-Sq, Mallows Cp. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat462/node/197/

questions.clue:
SSEₚ / MSEfull − n + 2p
p counts the subset model’s coefficients, including its intercept.
questions.explanation: Mallows’ Cp scales residual error by a full-model variance estimate and adjusts for complexity.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 462, §11.3, Best Subsets Regression, Adjusted R-Sq, Mallows Cp. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat462/node/197/

questions.clue:
Σⱼ(Q̂ⱼ − Q̄)² / (m−1)
Q̂ⱼ are estimates from m completed datasets, Q̄ their mean.
questions.explanation: This is the sample variance across the separately fitted estimates.
questions.reference: Duke University, Missing Data lecture, Missing data mechanisms and methods. https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~fl35/teaching/440-19F/decks/cs05_2_deck.html

questions.clue:
Σⱼ yᵢⱼ / pᵢⱼ, divided by m
m independent draws with replacement, per-draw probabilities p.
questions.explanation: The estimator averages each draw’s contribution using its per-draw selection probability.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 506, Lesson 3, Unequal Probability Sampling. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat506/Lesson03

questions.clue: The list that makes population units available for selection.
questions.explanation: The frame identifies the units through which the design can reach the population.
questions.reference: Everitt and Skrondal (2010), 4th ed., p. 377, Sampling frames

questions.clue: Which companion file records field meanings, units, and special missing-value codes?
questions.explanation: A codebook makes the same data fields interpretable to another analyst.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley Survey Documentation and Analysis, Help: Subsetting in SDA, Codebook. https://sda.berkeley.edu/sdaweb/helpfiles/helpsub.htm

questions.clue: A blank survey answer is filled with a donor value from a previous survey wave.
questions.explanation: Cold-deck imputation uses a donor source external to the current set of responses.
questions.reference: UCLA Office of Advanced Research Computing, Advanced Topics in Survey Data Analysis, Survey imputation. https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/other/mult-pkg/seminars/advanced-topics-in-survey-data-analysis/

questions.clue: A stratum has 30% of the population. A fixed-size stratified design gives it 30% of the sample slots.
questions.explanation: Proportional allocation gives each stratum the same sampling fraction.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 506, §6.1, Stratified Sampling. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat506/Lesson06

questions.clue: The same fold scores choose a tuning setting and report accuracy. What adds an independent evaluation loop?
choices: Leave-one-out with the same tuning loop
questions.explanation: An outer held-out fold evaluates the tuning procedure performed inside it.
questions.reference: University of Michigan, Biomedical Physics with Applications to Disease, Chapter 8, Honest validation and nested cross-validation. https://socr.umich.edu/BPAD1/BPAD1_notes/BPAD1_Chap08_DataModeling_AI_ML_part1.html

questions.clue: Fit incomplete data by alternating expected complete-data log likelihood with an update maximizing it.
questions.explanation: The E-step forms a conditional expectation and the M-step maximizes the resulting objective.
questions.reference: Duke University STA 440, Missing Data (2), The EM algorithm. https://www2.stat.duke.edu/courses/Spring25/sta440.001/slides/missing-data-2.html

questions.clue:
nₕ ∝ Nₕ Sₕ
Within strata, unit sampling costs are equal. Sₕ is the outcome standard deviation.
questions.explanation: At equal unit cost, allocation proportional to size times spread minimizes the stratified mean’s variance.
questions.reference: Penn State STAT 506, §6.1, Stratified Sampling. https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat506/Lesson06
